task.goal: Produce a multi-slide aspirational 'wishlist' carousel where a single recurring title lockup ('I wish my [X] looked like this') is paired across a run of grid/triptych slides, each carrying one grouped cluster of curated items or looks, building category-specific desire momentum slide over slide.
task.success_condition: The title lockup renders with identical wording, weight, and placement on every grid slide; each slide's image cluster shares exactly one coherent visual category (a single garment type, one outfit-fit triptych, or one aesthetic); the source handle attribution is legible on every branded slide; and a viewer swiping at speed still reads each slide as part of the same running list rather than a series of disconnected posts.
task.atomic_boundary: One curated wishlist theme becomes one multi-slide (typically 6-10 slide) grid carousel using a single repeating caption lockup over swapped item clusters. No cross-slide narrative arc, no video or motion, no single-frame quote graphic, and no unrelated bonus-content slide folded into the same list without a clear, separately-scoped category break.

source_expression_moment.description: The wishlist theme or aesthetic category the grid slides organize around (e.g. a closet capsule, a room edit, a shelf).

voice_context.description: Source handle/voice and caption-lockup reference used for rendering decisions.

carousel_slide_sequence.description: An ordered set of production-ready slide frames sharing one repeating title lockup, each carrying a single item/outfit cluster and creator attribution.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer's feed is saturated with wishlist and 'get ready with me' carousels competing for a half-second swipe decision. This one must earn the swipe-through by keeping the item cluster tightly curated to one visual category per slide, not by escalating into unrelated bonus content or reward-style claims bolted onto the list.
activative_input.stance: Peer-voice, aspirational, undecorated caption over grouped product or outfit imagery.
stakes: the list reads as a generic ad grid instead of a curated personal wishlist
the recurring caption becomes wallpaper and stops earning the next swipe
the format is used to smuggle in deceptive reward or 'glitch' claims that were never part of the wishlist premise
identity_urges: see my own taste reflected in someone else's curation
complete the mental collection by swiping to the next slide
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer reads the same short caption once, carries it as the frame for every subsequent slide, and taps through the grid comparing clusters against their own closet or space; save or share is the completion action, not a link click.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer saves or shares the carousel as a personal mood-board reference and follows the source handle for more curated lists, not because they were promised a discount, glitch, or survey reward.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not carry forward the 'site glitch' / 'link in bio' reward-claim framing present in two of the ten reference specimens (05.jpg, 09.jpg) -- this format is a curated wishlist grid, not a vehicle for implying a discount glitch, survey reward, or bonus giveaway the viewer must click through for.
Do not vary the repeating title lockup's wording or drop it from any grid slide -- a wishlist carousel that loses its one consistent caption reads as an unrelated product ad, not a running list.

Do not let the item cluster on a single slide mix multiple visual categories (e.g. tops with jeans with dresses) -- each slide's grid or triptych must stay to one coherent category, or the 'list' structure collapses into a random product dump.

Do not strip or obscure the source creator's handle/attribution overlaid on the grid -- presenting sourced product or outfit photography as the operator's own original content misattributes the wishlist's actual curator.
